title: Reuse validated coordinates for canonical semantic-key checks
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView construction already loads each SparseTensorEntry.coordinates tuple to validate exact axis binding and declared labels. Canonical-order validation then called SparseTensorEntry.semantic_key, which reread the same coordinates tuple solely to pair it with relation for the adjacent semantic-claim comparison.
primary_claim: TensorView canonical construction now reuses the coordinates tuple already loaded and validated in the current entry pass when forming the semantic claim key. Canonical retained entries therefore require one coordinates attribute read per entry instead of two while preserving the existing coordinate/relation uniqueness and ordering semantics.
gardener_decision: Reuse the already validated local coordinates binding in the existing entry-validation pass rather than introducing a cache, helper key object, parallel index or second Tensor representation. Keep SparseTensorEntry.semantic_key as the external reusable semantic-key surface for paths that do not already hold validated coordinates.
acceptance: canonical TensorView construction reads each retained entry coordinates attribute once during the validation/order pass
the semantic ordering key remains exactly (coordinates, relation)
canonical entry tuples remain retained by identity
non-canonical fallback ordering remains based on SparseTensorEntry.semantic_key
the Fourfold-v2 workflow executes successfully on the exact code/test revision
the designated Python 3.12/hash-seed-0 Tensor/Forest diagnostic executes successfully
the isolated wheel build/install executes successfully
repository-wide evidence remains collection-only rather than a full-suite execution claim
no OwnerApproval, promotion, Gate transition, measured memory/latency improvement or benchmark superiority claim is created
